title: Position, stop and end-outline lamps (version 3.0.0)
scope_summary: Approves device types of front and rear position lamps, stop-lamps (categories S1–S4) and front and rear end-outline marker lamps, including variable-intensity versions, light source modules and interdependent lamp systems. Position and stop lamps are for vehicles of categories L, M, N, O and T; end-outline marker lamps are for categories M, N, O and T only.
scope_quote: This Regulation applies to: Front and rear position lamps and stop lamps for vehicles of categories L, M, N, O and T; and, End-outline marker lamps for vehicles of categories M, N, O and T.
applies_to_components: Category S3/S4 stop lamp mounted outside or inside (behind the rear window) the vehicle
Device comprising both a rear position lamp and a stop-lamp
Lamps for use in an assembly of two lamps (D)
Lamps with non-replaceable filament or LED light sources
Grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, including lamps reciprocally incorporated with a headlamp
relation_to_other_regulations: Definitions of UN Regulation No. 48 (installation of lighting and light-signalling devices), in its series of amendments in force at the time of application, apply to this Regulation.
Filament light source categories must be those of UN Regulation No. 37; standard (étalon) filament light sources refer to UN R37.
LED light source categories must be those of UN Regulation No. 128; standard (étalon) LED light sources refer to UN R128.

Grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated units may combine lamps approved under this Regulation or another Regulation, with a single approval mark covering several Regulations (e.g. headlamp regulations).
Approval number series currently 02; the 03 series of amendments does not require changes in the approval number.

defined_terms.definition: The lamp used to indicate the presence and the width of the vehicle when viewed from the front.
The lamp used to indicate the presence and the width of the vehicle when viewed from the rear.
The lamp used to indicate to other road-users to the rear of the vehicle that its driver is applying the service brake, which may also be activated by a retarder or similar device.

A lamp fitted near the extreme outer edges and as close as possible to the top of the vehicle to indicate clearly the vehicle's overall width, complementing the position lamps on certain power-driven vehicles and trailers.

Front and rear position lamps, stop-lamps and end-outline marker lamps differing in trade name or mark, optical system characteristics (intensity, distribution angles, light source category, light source module) or variable intensity control, but not merely in colour of light source or filter.

applicability_hints: A rear combination lamp containing tail/position and stop functions is covered (combined R-S marking), even when grouped with lamps approved under other Regulations such as direction indicators or fog lamps.
Front position lamps integrated (reciprocally incorporated) into a headlamp fall under this Regulation for the position-lamp function.

A centre high-mounted/additional stop lamp (category S3/S4) is covered, including when mounted inside the vehicle behind the rear window; the rear window glazing optical properties then form part of the application.
Lamps using LED or other non-replaceable light sources and light source modules are covered; modules themselves must bear an 'MD' identification code.
An external electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control that is part of the lamp but not inside its body must carry manufacturer name and identification number.
Lamps with variable luminous intensity (R2, RM2, S2, S4) require the variable intensity control or a signal generator to be submitted.
Interdependent lamp systems (multiple units together performing one function) are covered and all units must be submitted by the same applicant.
Applies to motorcycles/mopeds (L) and agricultural tractors (T) and trailers (O) for position and stop lamps, but end-outline marker lamps are not in scope for L-category.
Changing only the light source colour or filter colour does not create a new type; extension for different light colour may keep the same approval number.
A stop-lamp may also be activated by a retarder or similar device, still under this Regulation.
Installation on the vehicle is governed by UN R48, not by this Regulation.
